newsitem.title: UK: LME traders play down tax meeting implications.
newsitem.headline: LME traders play down tax meeting implications.

text.p: A recent meeting of UK Inland Revenue's Special Compliance Office (SCO) and London Metal Exchange (LME) member companies was seen by market sources as no more than a warning shot by the taxman.
Some press reports suggested a massive tax probe was underway which could provide further embarassment for LME in the wake of last year's Sumitomo copper market scandal.
A brief statement from LME last week confirmed it arranged for a presentation to be made to members on May 15, at which SCO would explain its role, responsibilities and interests.
Those attending the meeting were asked that its content remain confidential. This prevented a clear picture emerging.

"As far as I hear the meeting appeared to target the 'local' trading system (traders dealing for personal gain) and explained the regulations that they should be aware of," a trader at a company which attended the meeting said.
"I believe those present were made fully aware of the consequences of abusing the system,' the trader added.

Market sources also said London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE), where there is a large 'local' membership, already had an information meeting with SCO and that International Petroleum Exchange will also be visited.
Neither exchange could confirm this. But one senior trade source said that each year the Inland Revenue selects a different occupation to take a detailed look.
"One year it is taxi drivers, the next it is something else. This year they have decided to look at dealers," he said.
A spokesman for Inland Revenue could not confirm or deny any of the rumours.
"What they said didn't come from our office because we can't say anything about investigations," he said.
One report suggested the taxman's visit to the LME had been triggered by Serious Fraud Office (SFO) enquiries into the $1.8 billion loss by a Sumitomo metal trader in the copper market last year.
An SFO spokesman said "It's not something we've got any direct involvement in."
